svg.text: OMS (orders) · IAS (inventory) · Payment · Search · Kafka with outbox + CDC — Postgres is the single source of truth, no Redis lock
15 · GET /search → results show AVAILABLE or RESERVED (held + booked). Seat-map screen is fetched live from IAS, not ES.
owns the order lifecycle · Postgres · talks sync to IAS & Payment
each state change = 1 txn: orders row + outbox row
Recon job: PAYMENT_PENDING > N min → poll gateway
Expiry job: SEAT_HELD past TTL → EXPIRED + release
user pays on hosted page · UPI / card
POST /seats/hold {orderId, seats[], ttl} — SYNC, idempotent, atomic check + hold
POST /seats/release {orderId} — payment failed / user cancelled / expiry job
POST /seats/confirm {orderId} — after webhook SUCCESS (also for late payments)
owns seat state · one row per (bus, date, seat) · Postgres
idempotent on orderId · multi-seat = 1 txn, sorted by seat_no
rows pre-generated when a trip is scheduled
→ writes SeatReleased to outbox (version+1) for Search / ES
approx seats-left; real seat map = IAS
Debezium CDC reads outbox tables → at-least-once; consumers idempotent
→ email / SMS / push with ticket + PNR
Search results (ES): approximate "seats left", eventually consistent.
Seat-map screen: GET /seatmap from IAS (authoritative; optional Redis cache, never a lock).
The hold call is the final authority — the UI may be stale, the DB is not.
OMS→IAS: timeouts + circuit breaker. On timeout, retry with the same orderId (idempotent) or GET /holds/{orderId} to learn the truth.
Webhook is the source of truth (redirect result is only a hint). Dedupe by gateway_ref; recon job covers lost webhooks.
Outbox in BOTH OMS and IAS removes the DB-write + Kafka-publish dual-write problem.
If a seat was held, OMS calls IAS release(orderId)

g.text: • Every transition = ONE txn (orders row + outbox row)
• Optimistic lock: UPDATE … WHERE order_id=? AND version=?
• Late webhook SUCCESS on an EXPIRED order → PAID → confirm():
seat still free → CONFIRMED · seat taken → SEAT_LOST → refund
• Recon job polls gateway for PAYMENT_PENDING > N min
• Refund is idempotent and tracked in the refunds table

svg.text: late confirm (expired but unclaimed): AVAILABLE → BOOKED

g.text: WHERE bus_id=:b AND travel_date=:d AND seat_no=:s
-- SWEEP: batch UPDATE … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED → AVAILABLE
-- multi-seat: one txn, ORDER BY seat_no (deadlock-free)
-- UI timer 8m < hold TTL 10m: no race on last-second pay
hold OK → pay → webhook SUCCESS → confirm → CONFIRMED → notify + ES update
Gateway FAILED / user cancels → PAYMENT_FAILED → release() immediately
User still on pay page? keep hold till TTL so they can retry (short grace)
No webhook, TTL lapses → seat lazily AVAILABLE → order EXPIRED
Sweeper flips row + emits SeatReleased → Search / ES catches up
Payment PENDING, TTL expires, late webhook
PENDING: never release early; wait for webhook / recon poll until TTL
TTL gone + late SUCCESS → confirm(): seat free → BOOKED → CONFIRMED
seat taken by user2 → SEAT_LOST → refund user1 (idempotent) → REFUNDED
Two users, same seat, same instant
Both run the conditional UPDATE; Postgres row lock serializes them
winner rows=1 → HELD · loser rows=0 → 409 → HOLD_FAILED (no Redis lock)
hold() timeout → retry same orderId (idempotent) or GET /holds/{orderId}
duplicate webhook / confirm → no-op, same result; dedupe by gateway_ref
User → OMS: POST /orders (seat S1, bus B1, day D1)
OMS → IAS: POST /hold (sync, atomic check + hold)
IAS: conditional UPDATE → HELD + expires_at (+ outbox row)
Payment → Gateway; user pays on hosted page (UPI / card)
IAS: HELD → BOOKED, sync 200 (+ outbox SeatBooked)
Notification Service consumes → email / SMS / push
Search Consumer → versioned upsert into Elasticsearch
Search Service → User: AVAILABLE / RESERVED flags
Fail / cancel / expiry → OMS → IAS /release → AVAILABLE
REST/gRPC for hold / confirm / release: the user waits and needs a
definite yes/no. Kafka only for fan-out (Search, Notifications).
Postgres row lock + conditional UPDATE already prevents double booking.
Redis adds a 2nd source of truth + cleanup burden. Use only as cache.
Lazy expiry inside the hold/read query = correctness.
Sweeper (30-60s, SKIP LOCKED) = hygiene + SeatReleased events.
Webhook = truth; recon job covers lost webhooks. Outbox on both sides.
ES is eventually consistent; IAS is the final authority on seats.
